publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Challenges in the Treatment of Chronic Wounds

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: chronic wounds - a category defined by a failure to heal in a `timely manner` whose timescale the definition does not state
span.quote: Chronic wounds are defined as wounds that fail to proceed through the normal phases of wound healing in an orderly and timely manner.

span.label: what makes these wounds fail to heal, and which of the available therapies the evidence actually supports
span.quote: However, selection of an appropriate therapy is often not evidence based.

span.label: a review of the pathophysiology and the treatment modalities, unusually explicit that therapy selection is often not evidence based
span.quote: More evidence for the efficacy of current and future advanced wound therapies is required for their appropriate use.

span.label: critique
span.quote: However, selection of an appropriate therapy is often not evidence based.

span.label: wounds that stall - typically in the inflammation phase - and share molecular features across etiologies that differ from one another
span.quote: Despite differences in etiology at the molecular level, chronic wounds share certain common features, including excessive levels of proinflammatory cytokines, proteases, ROS, and senescent cells, as well as the existence of persistent infection, and a deficiency of stem cells that are often also dysfunctional

span.label: narrative review of chronic wound pathophysiology and of each therapeutic modality against the trial evidence for it
span.term: narrative review of chronic wound pathophysiology and of each therapeutic modality against the trial evidence for it
span.quote: Nonetheless, RCTs are still required to evaluate the clinical efficacy of this modality in healing chronic wounds of different etiologies.

span.label: chronic wounds stall in the INFLAMMATION phase and share excessive proinflammatory cytokines, proteases, reactive oxygen species and senescent cells, plus persistent infection and a deficiency of stem cells - shared features DESPITE differing etiology
span.quote: Despite differences in etiology at the molecular level, chronic wounds share certain common features, including excessive levels of proinflammatory cytokines, proteases, ROS, and senescent cells, as well as the existence of persistent infection, and a deficiency of stem cells that are often also dysfunctional

span.label: AND THE CAUSES DO NOT CONVERGE: the underlying pathologies that make these wounds fail to heal DIFFER among the various types, so the shared molecular signature does not imply a shared cause
span.quote: Underlying pathologies, which result in the failure of these wounds to heal, differ among various types of chronic wounds.

span.label: THE DEFINITION IS A NEGATIVE ONE WITH THE CLOCK LEFT OUT: chronic wounds are wounds that FAIL TO PROCEED through normal healing `in an orderly and TIMELY MANNER`, and the definition never says how long timely is
span.quote: Chronic wounds are defined as wounds that fail to proceed through the normal phases of wound healing in an orderly and timely manner.

span.label: the extent is left open too - `include, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED, TO` diabetic foot ulcers, venous leg ulcers and pressure ulcers - so neither the intension nor the extension is bounded, in the abstract's first sentence
span.quote: Chronic wounds include, but are not limited, to diabetic foot ulcers, venous leg ulcers, and pressure ulcers. They are a challenge to wound care professionals and consume a great deal of healthcare resources around the globe.

span.label: THE FIELD SAYS ITS PRACTICE OUTRUNS ITS EVIDENCE, IN ITS OWN ABSTRACT: `selection of an appropriate therapy is OFTEN NOT EVIDENCE BASED`
span.quote: However, selection of an appropriate therapy is often not evidence based.

span.label: and again in the closing: more evidence for the efficacy of current AND FUTURE advanced wound therapies is required for their appropriate use
span.quote: More evidence for the efficacy of current and future advanced wound therapies is required for their appropriate use.

span.label: a named case of use without evidence: topical wound oxygen is `highly controversial`, its lack of a formal study `offset by` reviews and case series, and there have been NO PUBLICATIONS comparing 12-week healing rates with standard care
span.quote: While several RCTs with different devices have been ongoing, there have been no publications to date comparing 12-week healing rates with those of standard care.

span.label: each modality is assessed against whether a comparison with STANDARD CARE exists, rather than against whether studies support it
span.note: eliminates: a therapy accumulating favourable case series and reviews and being read as established - the review states for topical oxygen that no publication compares 12-week healing rates with standard care · outcome: failed
span.quote: the use of topical wound oxygen for DFUs and VLUs has been considered as highly controversial, especially by advocates of HBOT. The lack of a formal study in this regard has been offset by several reviews, case series, and experimental studies on the effect of topically administered oxygen at the wound surface that seem to indicate a benefit in promoting wound repair.

span.label: the 4-week reassessment rule: if standard care has not produced sufficient healing, the underlying pathology is re-examined before advanced agents are considered
span.note: eliminates: an advanced therapy being credited with a healing that a missed underlying pathology was preventing · outcome: absent-declared-unreported
span.quote: When wounds fail to achieve sufficient healing after 4 weeks of standard care, reassessment of underlying pathology and consideration of the need for advanced therapeutic agents should be undertaken.

span.label: whether the shared molecular signature implies a shared cause across wound types
span.note: eliminates: nothing - the review states the underlying pathologies DIFFER among types, and asks for a better understanding of those differences · outcome: failed
span.quote: Despite differences in etiology at the molecular level, chronic wounds share certain common features, including excessive levels of proinflammatory cytokines, proteases, ROS, and senescent cells, as well as the existence of persistent infection, and a deficiency of stem cells that are often also dysfunctional

span.label: chronic wound - AS DEFINED HERE, BY WHAT IT FAILS TO DO: a wound that does not proceed through the normal phases of healing in an orderly and timely manner. The defining property is a RATE, and no rate is given
span.quote: Chronic wounds are defined as wounds that fail to proceed through the normal phases of wound healing in an orderly and timely manner.

span.label: `timely manner` - AND THE ONLY NUMBER THE PAPER ATTACHES TO IT IS A DECISION RULE, NOT A DEFINITION: at 4 weeks of standard care without sufficient healing, reassess and consider advanced agents. FOUR WEEKS IS WHEN YOU CHANGE TREATMENT, NOT WHEN THE WOUND BECOMES CHRONIC - and the paper does not claim otherwise, which is the honest version of this gap
span.quote: When wounds fail to achieve sufficient healing after 4 weeks of standard care, reassessment of underlying pathology and consideration of the need for advanced therapeutic agents should be undertaken.

span.label: the shared signature - chronic wounds of different etiologies share a molecular profile AND have different underlying pathologies. The category holds together at the level the assay reads and comes apart at the level that causes it
span.quote: Underlying pathologies, which result in the failure of these wounds to heal, differ among various types of chronic wounds.

span.label: critiques → current wound-care practice, on the ground that selection of an appropriate therapy is often not evidence based
span.quote: However, selection of an appropriate therapy is often not evidence based.

span.label: critiques → topical wound oxygen for diabetic foot and venous leg ulcers, whose supporting literature is reviews and case series rather than a comparison against standard care
span.quote: While several RCTs with different devices have been ongoing, there have been no publications to date comparing 12-week healing rates with those of standard care.

span.label: critiques → extracorporeal shock wave therapy as an established modality - RCTs are still required to evaluate its clinical efficacy
span.quote: Nonetheless, RCTs are still required to evaluate the clinical efficacy of this modality in healing chronic wounds of different etiologies.
